Title: Limited research
Description: Just a simple research. Web searching, AI asking and putting it all together in a dataset.

Title: Customer focus research
Description: Who is your main customer? Who will benefit from your service? How can you deliver a value?

Title: Technical focus research
Description: How to make what you wana make? What technologies would you use? How can they work together?

Title: Full scale research
Description: You throw all your resources and efforts to make your product the best fit possible. It will help in a long run... probably.

Title: Essential prototype
Description: This prototipe will just show that your idea works. It is ugly. It is buggy. But it proves the very basic concept.

Title: Service prototype
Description: This isn't a technical prototype. You have your landing page up and running, and you should do everything else by hand with every client.

Title: Technical prototype
Description: Now you know, that everything is working on the technical side. User experience? Never heard about this.

Title: Product MVP
Description: This MVP proves everything and you can ship it to selected audience. It is well designed. Well built. And it took time and effort to make it this early.

Title: Mission only
Description: Now your crew knows why are you doing what you are doing.

Title: Values and Strategy
Description: Values will help your team to make important decisions. Strategy will navigate them on which decisions they should make.

Title: Values and Mission
Description: Values will help your team to make important decisions. Mission will give them purpose to make these decisions.

Title: Values, Mission and Strategy
Description: You have done it all. Now your team knows why, how, and which decisions they should make. It invokes confidence.

Title: Internal testing
Description: Your team and friends are enough to test your product. There is no need to gather the audience.

Title: Medium focus group testing
Description: Your testing group consists of a few dozens of people both from your audience and new ones. It will help to catch criticals in your product.

Title: Real-world testing
Description: It is relatively good idea to just put your product online and acquire some users to simply use it. If you are ready to rapidly fix all appearing problems.

Title: Cascade testing with user groups
Description: Full-scale testing with several stages, each bigger. You have prepared and made it all

Title: Website building
Description: You definitely need a website. Anything else? Probaply, not.

Title: Social media setup
Description: Who needs a website when you can make it all with a proper social media account?

Title: Website and Social Media
Description: It is often easier to gather audience via social media, but they should be landed somewhere.

Title: Full marketing commitment
Description: Social media, website, community hub, press releases, and contacts with influencers. You should have it all to succeed.

Title: Single server
Description: Simple backand will be more then enough. So why bother and spend additional money on an ifrastructure? What could possibly go wrong?

Title: Cloud infrastructure
Description: Why should we bother to make our own server if we can use a cloud? It is a little bit more expensive, but definitely much more convenient.

Title: Multiple servers
Description: We know how to make it on our own with all the redundancy we need to provide a consistent service to our clients.

Title: DevOPS team with an infrastructure
Description: Infrastructure needs to be carfully planned and maintained. So we need to hire a DevOPS team to help use make this project.

Title: Self application
Description: Just prepare all the documents and send it according to instructions on a DPG website.

Title: Contact DPG office to assist
Description: We can make it with the DPG office, if they are able to help.

Title: Address SDG relevance only
Description: You have checked if your product is SDG relevant or not. If it is - so why bother? It will work anyway.

Title: DPG indicator checklist
Description: You have your checklist, so you go thugh all 9 indicators and prepare properly your application.

Title: Release marketing campaign
Description: Your team is fully focused on a marketing campaign for the release. The technical side of things is not in focus.

Title: Release event
Description: Just throw a release event to attract an audience. They will watch the stream and then they will use your product.

Title: Some release preparations
Description: You clearly have not enough time to make it all, but you can address the majore issues and prepare the campaign on a decent level.

Title: Full scale release preparations
Description: Your team is working on the release, giving attention to everything. It will take time. But since you have one, you can afford it.

Title: Essential support only
Description: We don't have enough resources for the full scale support, so we will do only bare essentials.

Title: Phone and email customer support
Description: We will conduct a customer support via both phone and email.

Title: Support with LiveOPS
Description: We will not only make a support up and running, but also establish regular events and activities for our clients (LiveOPS).

Title: Outsourced support
Description: We no need our team to make a customer support. Let's hire an outsource company to make it for us!

Title: Limited Research
Description: You study existing air pollution reports and national health statistics, ask AI about the problem, staying at home drinking hot chocolate and listening to music. This is really convenient, but the data might be not accurate.

Title: Local Research
Description: You plan to spend your weekend asking people in your district about the problem of air pollution in the city by giving out polls and questionnaires. The best thing about it is that you only need to lose only one weekend of yours.

Title: Technical Research
Description: You focus on which phones people use and the signal coverage. It will allow you to ensure the project will be used by as many people as possible, but it won't consider how they feel about using it.

Title: Full Scale Research
Description: You spend weeks across different city districts and places by conducting interviews and pulling questionnaires. A few data analysts will be hired to help create the right questionnaires and analyze the data. It is very expensive and slow, yet it gives many insightful results.

Title: Social Media Post
Description: You decided to make a post about your project to raise more attention. It is fast, but there might be few people who will stop scrolling and read the post.

Title: University Speech
Description: You're invited to give a speech at university for students about your project. The chances your project will gain more followers is high.

Title: Radio Station Speech
Description: After telling your friend, who works at a small radio station, about the project, he invites you to talk about the app before it even exists. After the speech, only middle-aged and old people will find out about your project.

Title: Fair Exhibition
Description: You decided to go the fair where young entrepreneurs speech their projects to gain more recognition. It is good, but the fair is mainly dedicated to commercial products.

Title: GoFundMe Post
Description: You think that it will be a great idea to raise more funds for the development by crowdsourcing. The chances your project will be noticed are little, yet you can give it a shot.

Title: Choosing Local District
Description: You decided to measure air quality in your district only because it would cost much to collect data from all districts. The amount of data is less, but its quality is high.

Title: Budget Review
Description: You decide to plan how you will spend your budget to ensure the current amount of money is enough for the project. It takes effort and money, but it will be useful in the future.

Title: Plan Creation
Description: You don't think that your product needs attention because you haven't created anything yet, so you decide to put your hands on the development by writing technical specification to define the project's structure.

Title: Paper Prototype
Description: You sketch every screen on paper and test it by hand with people outside. It is cheap and fast. It takes time and effort, yet the results will be poor.

Title: Video Prototype
Description: You consider creating a video with photos of the project and disseminate the video on social media to gather the users' thoughts. It takes less time to disseminate and lets more people look at the project.

Title: Digital Prototype
Description: You create a polished and tappable MVP. It looks more professional to investors and people. It takes effort, but the results might be really good.

Title: Co-design Workshops
Description: You DM your city professionals to meet at the weekends to create the app together. Slow and costly, but it will allow you to create a better application.

Title: Elderly User Testing
Description: You realize your application might be hard to use by elderly, so you ask your grandparents to test the application to get insights into what problems old people might encounter while ussing the app.

Title: Adding Languages
Description: People from your city speak three languages. Currently, your application supports only one of them, so you plan on adding two more languages on the application.

Title: Application Dissemination
Description: You think that more people should be aware of your application, regardless of its current flaws, which can be fixed later. Therefore, you buy advertisement campaigns on different social platforms.

Title: Performance Issues
Description: You notice that your application is working really slow. You decide to spend more time on optimizing existing features rather than adding extra ones.

Title: Outsource to Junior Developers
Description: You pay a little amount of money to junior developers. The code will be messy, the features might stop working after updates, but the price is pretty low.

Title: Outsource to Professional Developers
Description: You pay a professional team much money to build it fast. The code is reliable, but the additional features might not be implemented due to high costs.

Title: Core Features Only
Description: Browse air-quality at the current district, without any additional metrics.

Title: Full Feature Build
Description: Browse air-quality at the current district for the specified time, with additional metrics about which gases pollute the air and their percentage.

Title: Overlooked User Need
Description: You've launched your MVP, but you constantly get reports from the users about particular features not implemented making the application uncomfortable to use. You decide to spend time on their development.

Title: Partnership Opportunity
Description: A small team of entrepreneurs noticed your project and offers co-fund the next phase in exchange for input on the app's direction and a seat at your table.

Title: Database Deduplication
Description: While browsing the database, you notice there are multiple duplicate entries which shouldn't be repeated. You plan to spend time on fixing the issue.

Title: IOS Optimization
Description: You've obtained multiple reports from users using the application on their IOS about application crashing, so you want to find the root cause and fix it.

Title: Adding More Neighborhoods
Description: People complain about not being able to monitor the air quality of their district, so you decide to add all city district in your application. It will take much time, yet there will be more new users.

Title: Government Contract
Description: The city government is intersted in your project and it asks your team to create a private application for monitoring the air quality of a military base. Take into account you will have to maintain two distinct apps if you agree.

Title: Power Plant Agreement
Description: The power plant employees notice that they are the main contributors to the air pollution in the region and they ask you to remove them from the application database to save their reputation. Should you do it?

Title: Data Source Switch
Description: The fire hit the database building of the company that provided the up-to-date air quality information. This is the reason why the information in your app is not updated that often. You can make an agreement with another company to provide the data to improve the customer service, but switching will take much time.

Title: Big Company Acquisition
Description: The large city company saw a monetary potential in your application, so it wants to purchase all your company's shares to own it.

Title: Further Development
Description: You have many innovative ideas regarding your project. You decide to work further on the project and helping more and more people.

Title: Changing Business Goals
Description: Your initial goal was to build a DPG. Now, you notice how many people and companies want to use your app, and you decide to switch the project's strategy from DPG to a commercial product. This choice might have great consequences.

Title: Give up on Project
Description: You've done a great work, but you realize how hard it is to be an entrepreneur, so you want to hand over all your responsibilities to another person and quit the project.
